entry.name: mc.range~
entry.digest: Generate a multichannel signal with a range of constant values
entry.description: The mc.range~ object generates a multichannel signal filled with constant values distributed across a defined range.

arguments.name: size
arguments.description: Sets the number of channels in the multichannel output.

attributes.digest: Number of Channels
attributes.description: Theattribute sets the channel count of the output multichannel signal, determining the number of channels that will be used to define the range. Ifis modified while the audio is on, extra channels are set to zero. After audio is restarted, the output channel count will be set to the value of.

attributes.name: inclusive
attributes.digest: Include Range Endpoints
attributes.description: Determines how endpoint values are used when calculating values for each output channel.

choices.label: Uses neither the low or high endpoint values when calculating mc channel values. For example, 5 channels with aof 0.0 and aof 1.0 will generate signal values of 0.17, 0.33, 0.5, 0.67, and 0.83.

Uses the low enpoint value for the first channel and high endpoint value as the last channel when calculating mc channel values. For example, 5 channels with aof 0.0 and aof 1.0 will generate signal values of 0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, and 1.0.

Uses the low endpoint value for the first channel and calculates all other channel values accordingly. For example, 5 channels with aof 0.0 and aof 1.0 will generate signal values of 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, and 0.8.

Uses the high endpoint value for the last channel and calculates all other channel values accordingly. For example, 5 channels with aof 0.0 and aof 1.0 will generate signal values of 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, and 1.0.

attributes.name: reflection
attributes.digest: Reflection Point
attributes.description: Theattribute sets a relative location within the range where the output reaches its high value and then returns to the low value. By default, the value ofis 1 which has no effect on the output range. Ifis set to a value between 0 and 1, the output reaches the high value somewhere in the middle of the output channel space, returning to the low value for the last channel in the output multichannel signal. Asmoves toward zero, the output begins to resemble an inverted range and whenis set to 0, the output is completely inverted.
